coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 only (130–140 bpm based on your recent avg HR). You're 32 days out, in taper, and your resting HR is 4 bpm above your 30-day average—a signal you're still carrying fatigue from the peak block. Monday is a recovery day anyway; use it to flush legs and keep the aerobic engine ticking without adding stress. If you feel flat, dial it back to 5 miles or skip the run entirely. You don't lose fitness in taper; you lose it by not respecting what your body is telling you.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're sleeping 90 minutes less than your monthly average (6.9h vs. 8.05h), which means your glycogen stores and nervous system recovery are already compromised. Prioritize carbs today: aim for 6–8 grams per kilogram of body weight spread across meals and snacks. Post-run, hit 30–40g carbs + 15–20g protein within 30 minutes to cap glycogen depletion. With travel and a packed schedule, this is non-negotiable in taper—you can't manufacture sleep overnight, but you can feed recovery aggressively.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your recovery score is 52/100 (moderate) and sleep efficiency is solid at 93.3%, but absolute volume is the problem—you need 8+ hours tonight, not 6.9. This is your #1 lever right now. No screens after 21:00, cool room (≤65°F if possible), black-out shades. You've got 32 days to race; four weeks of genuine sleep debt will cost you more than any missed interval session. Treat sleep like a workout you can't skip.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper paranoia is real, and it hits executives hard because you're used to controlling outcomes through work. You've already earned your fitness—31 miles last week in a build/peak block proves that. The next 32 days are about arriving at Kranjska Gora fresh, not fit. Your job is to execute the taper structure (easy volume, no hard intensity), sleep, fuel, and trust the work. The Alps demand mental clarity on vert; you'll get that by resting now, not by squeezing in extra miles.
